description: The larval stage (caterpillar) of sphinx moths is commonly called hornworm. It is large, smooth-bodied, often with a horn-like projection at the posterior end.
damage: Feeding on leaves, stems, and sometimes fruit of host plants
Defoliation can occur if populations are high
Leaves often have irregular holes or chewed edges
Can weaken young plants and reduce yield in crops such as tomato, tobacco, and other Solanaceae
control: Biological control with Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) or parasitic wasps
Use of row covers for young plants
Encouraging natural predators like birds and predatory insects
notes: Sphinx moth larvae are often confused with other large caterpillars; look for the horn at the posterior end.
Management focuses mainly on larval stage, as adults are beneficial pollinators.
